instructions: At least 2 hours ahead, or the night before: peel and devein the shrimp if they aren't already, and cut each one into 3 pieces.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil, then turn it down to a simmer. Add the shrimp, cover and take the pot off the heat. Let them sit for about 2 minutes, until pink and no longer see-through.
Drain the shrimp and rinse them under cold water so they stop cooking.
Drain the octopus into a large bowl so the oil collects there, and cut the octopus into bite-sized pieces. Whisk the 2 tbsp olive oil and the 3 tbsp vinegar into the oil in the bowl.
Halve the tomatoes. Chop both peppers into 1/2 inch pieces. Roughly chop the olives to get 1/3 cup and finely chop 1/3 cup of the onion.
Add the shrimp, octopus, tomatoes, peppers, olives and onion to the bowl. Sprinkle in the salt and pepper and toss well.
Cover and chill for at least 2 hours, or overnight.
Give it a stir and serve it chilled with slices of the baguette. It keeps in the fridge for up to 1 day after mixing.
advance_prep_notes: chill for at least 2 hours, or overnight
method_notes: Goya's Salpicon de Mariscos poaches the shrimp briefly off the heat, tosses it with canned octopus in olive oil, tomatoes, peppers, olives and onion in a sherry vinegar and olive oil dressing, and chills it for at least 2 hours. Benidorm Seriously's version poaches fish, squid and mussels and uses lime and cilantro, and says to cook the seafood a day ahead. Neither shows a rating, so this is a fallback. Goya's amounts are for 6, so they're scaled to 4 (shrimp 1 lb down to 3/4 lb).
